methodology: Static trace of Next.js routes, auth flow, providers, API client, proxy route, and backend auth/control-plane routes.
Read-only runtime checks of running prod/staging containers, recent backend/frontend logs, HTTP timings, and PostgreSQL connection state.
No login POST was executed during this diagnostic to avoid creating a new auth session and audit-write side effects.

executive_summary.primary_root_cause: The current production backend is effectively wedged by DB connection pool exhaustion: PostgreSQL shows 15 idle-in-transaction connections, matching SQLAlchemy's default pool capacity of size 5 plus overflow 10. New requests wait for a connection and then fail after 30 seconds.
executive_summary.frontend_contribution: The frontend amplifies the backend bottleneck during auth and console boot by issuing duplicate provider fan-out requests with no client timeout, while route guards keep /login or protected pages in loading states until auth/provider requests resolve.
executive_summary.login_failure_root_cause: Login cannot reliably complete because the login flow requires both /auth/login and an immediate /auth/me revalidation. In the current prod state, auth/me does not return within 10 seconds and backend logs show 30 second pool timeouts. Additionally, prod/staging default to Secure cookies, so direct HTTP access on localhost-style ports will not persist the session cookie.
executive_summary.white_screen_or_loading_cause: The first browser render is blocked by guard state, not by the HTML response. /login HTML returned in about 16 ms, but PublicOnly hides the login form while AuthProvider waits on /auth/me; if /auth/me hangs, the login page remains a spinner.

root_cause_ranking_top_5.cause: Backend DB connection pool exhaustion with idle-in-transaction leak/saturation
evidence: Production backend logs show sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00.
PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity showed 15 idle in transaction connections plus active/background sessions.
Production /health and /api/backend/health did not return within 10 seconds, proving the issue is systemic and not only a business endpoint.
root_cause_ranking_top_5.impact: All auth/provider/API requests can hang or fail with 500 after 30 seconds. This directly explains slow loads, stuck auth checks, and login failure.

root_cause_ranking_top_5.cause: Frontend boot fan-out and duplicate provider requests
evidence: CapabilityStateProvider dispatches 9 parallel requests after authentication.
OperationsDashboard calls capability refresh again while also loading health, logs, approvals, and users.
root_cause_ranking_top_5.impact: A single dashboard load can multiply auth/session/permission checks, accelerating backend pool saturation and making slow API tails dominate first paint.

root_cause_ranking_top_5.cause: Repeated backend session validation and write amplification per request
evidence: Control-plane isolation, org context, permission isolation, data isolation, and route dependencies can each validate the session.
validate_session() updates last_seen and commits during read-heavy paths.
The prior PRE20-K report independently flagged this as high write amplification and row contention risk.
root_cause_ranking_top_5.impact: Provider fan-out becomes many DB sessions and commits per browser action, creating contention on auth_sessions and pressure on SQLAlchemy's pool.

root_cause_ranking_top_5.cause: Production/staging Secure session cookie over direct HTTP access
evidence: APP_ENV is production or staging and AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is not explicitly disabled, so backend defaults Secure=true.
Published local ports are http://127.0.0.1:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:3100.
Secure cookies are not persisted by browsers over plain HTTP.
root_cause_ranking_top_5.impact: When accessed through direct HTTP ports, /auth/login can return Set-Cookie but the browser drops it; the immediate /auth/me then returns unauthenticated.

root_cause_ranking_top_5.cause: Route guards and auth flow have no request timeout boundary
evidence: apiRequest() calls fetch without AbortController timeout.
PublicOnly returns only a spinner while auth status is checking.
LoginForm keeps isSubmitting true until login() resolves or rejects.
AuthProvider login() requires currentUserRequest() after loginRequest().
root_cause_ranking_top_5.impact: Backend hangs propagate directly into infinite-looking spinners, stuck Signing in state, and delayed redirects.

react_render_loop_analysis.conclusion: The render issue is not an infinite React loop. It is repeated legitimate rerendering driven by slow duplicated async provider loads.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Recover and inspect backend DB connection pool state: identify why sessions remain idle in transaction, close leaked sessions safely, and confirm health returns quickly before touching frontend.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: The current production system cannot serve even health/auth reliably while pool slots are consumed.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Audit backend middleware/session lifecycle: remove repeated per-request validate_session commits and ensure all middleware-created sessions are closed promptly.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: This is the backend source of pool/write amplification.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Add request timeout/cancellation boundaries around frontend apiRequest and provider loads.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: A backend hang should degrade to a bounded fallback/error state instead of infinite checking/signing-in.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Deduplicate console boot data: make CapabilityStateProvider the single source for module/adapter/execution-provider access or share a request cache.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: This reduces first-load fan-out and backend auth/permission checks.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Fix environment/access-mode mismatch: use HTTPS for production/staging access or explicitly configure non-secure cookies only for local non-production diagnostics.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: Secure cookies over direct HTTP make login appear to succeed but /auth/me fails.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Move dashboard refreshCapabilityState out of the first dashboard data load or make it use the already-loaded provider state.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: Avoids another 9-request capability fan-out during first dashboard render.

recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.recommendation: Add observability for provider/API boot timings and backend pool metrics.
recommended_fix_order_no_implementation.rationale: Future regressions should identify slow provider/API stages before users see blank/loading screens.
